basic_info: 43-year-old female presenting with pain in the top part of the right leg following a bowling incident.
present_illness: Pain onset during the incident, characterized by throbbing and aching, exacerbated by weight-bearing or touch. Bruising and mild swelling noted. No sharp pain. The pain has been a constant ache, especially when putting weight on it.
past_history: No prior injuries or surgeries to the right leg. History of atopic eczema and colectomy for diverticulitis. No diabetes, osteoporosis, or blood clotting disorders.
physical_exam: Tenderness localized to the top of the right leg, more on the side. No deformity, instability, numbness, tingling, weakness, warmth, redness, or skin color changes. Limited weight-bearing and difficulty walking.
aux_exam: Imaging studies: The patient mentioned that an X-ray was done today during the visit and was reviewed by a healthcare provider, who reported it as normal. The patient is unsure about the facility where it was performed and the name of the provider who reviewed it.
